  (3) The principal of a school shall report the state of performance of operation plan to the school governance committee at least once a year.

Article 5 (Composition of school meal services committee) (1) A school meal services committee provided in Article 5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "school meal services committee") shall be comprised of up to 15 members including a chairperson. <Amended on Jun. 28, 2022>
  (2) The deputy superintendent (referring to the first deputy superintendent in cases where there are two deputy superintendents) of the Office of Education in each Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as "Office of Education in City/Do") shall be the chairperson (hereinafter referred to as "chairperson") of each school meal services committee. <Amended on Jun. 28, 2022>

  (4) Every school meal services committee shall have one secretary, who shall be appointed by the chairperson from among the public officials of the Office of Education in City/Do. <Amended on Jun. 28, 2022>

Article 8-2 (Standards for placement of teachers in kindergartens) (1) Under the proviso of Article 7 (1) of the Act, at least one teacher qualified as a nutrition teacher (in cases of a national or public kindergarten, referring to a person selected as a nutrition teacher pursuant to Article 9 (1) of the Decree on the Appointment of Educational Officials) under Article 21 (2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act shall be placed at a national or public kindergarten provided in subparagraphs 1 and 2 of Article 7 of the Early Childhood Education Act (hereinafter referred to as "national or public kindergarten") and a private kindergarten with at least 100 children currently enrolled, in order to take charge of affairs provided in the subparagraphs of Article 8. <Amended on Jun. 28, 2022>
  (2) From among kindergartens required to have a nutrition teacher under paragraph (1), a kindergarten with less than 200 children currently enrolled may employ one teacher provided in paragraph (1) jointly with another such kindergarten within the jurisdiction of the same district office of education (referring to a district office of education under Article 34 (1) of the Local Education Autonomy Act and Article 80 (1) of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended on Jun. 28, 2022>
  (3) The Superintendent of the relevant Office of Education may require a nutrition teacher assigned to a City/Do office of education or a district office of education to support the management of meal services for kindergartens not required to employ a nutrition teacher under paragraphs (1) and (2) from among private kindergartens required to provide school meal services under subparagraph 1 of Article 4 of the Act and Article 2-2 of this Decree. <Added on Jun. 28, 2022>
  (4) A nutrition teacher assigned to a City/Do office of education or a district office of education pursuant to Article 7 (3) of the Act shall support the following matters for kindergartens referred to in paragraph (3): <Added on Jun. 28, 2022>
  1. Preparation of menu and nutrition management;
  2. Management of sanitation and safety;
  3. Guidance on dietary life and consultation on nutrition;
  4. Other matters deemed necessary by the superintendent of education to manage meal services for kindergartens.
  (5) When the superintendent of education assigns a nutrition teacher to a City/Do office of education or a district office of education pursuant to Article 7 (3) of the Act, he or she shall take into account the number of kindergartens, the distance between kindergartens, the number of children enrolled in each kindergarten, etc. <Added on Jun. 28, 2022>

Criteria for Imposition of Administrative Fines (Related to Article 18)
■ Enforcement Decree of the School Meals Act [Appendix] <Amended on Apr. 25, 2023>

Criteria for Imposition of Administrative Fines (Related to Article 18)

1. General Criteria
(a) The administrative-fine standards according to the number of violations shall apply where an administrative fine has been imposed for the same violation within the preceding three years. In such cases, the number of violations shall be calculated by reference to the date on which the administrative-fine disposition for the violation was imposed and the date on which the same violation was detected again, respectively.
(b) The imposing authority may reduce the amount of an administrative fine under subparagraph 2 by up to one half in any of the following cases. However, this shall not apply to a violator who is in arrears in paying administrative fines.
1) Where the violator falls under any subparagraph of Article 2-2 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Regulation of Violations of Public Order.
2) Where the violator has corrected or eliminated the consequences of the unlawful act.
3) Where the violation is recognized as having resulted from negligence, such as minor carelessness or an error.
4) Where the consequences of the violation are minor.
5) Where a reduction is otherwise deemed necessary in view of the degree of the violation, the motive for the violation, its consequences, and other relevant circumstances.
(c) Where a violator who has acted without intent or gross negligence is a micro enterprise under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Micro Enterprises and is not in arrears in paying administrative fines, the imposing authority may, taking the following matters into consideration, reduce the amount of the administrative fine under the individual criteria in subparagraph 2 by up to 70 percent. However, this reduction shall not be applied together with the reduction under item (b).
1) The violator's actual ability to bear the burden.
2) Whether conditions in the market or industry to which the violator belongs have changed markedly or have continued to deteriorate owing to an economic crisis or other circumstances.

2. Individual Criteria
Violation | Statutory basis | Administrative fine (unit: 10,000 won): first violation / second violation / third or subsequent violation
(a) Where a school meal service provider, despite receiving a corrective order under Article 19 (3) of the Act for violating Article 16 (2) 1 of the Act, fails to comply with it without just cause | Article 25 (1) of the Act | 100 / 300 / 500
(b) Where a school meal service provider, despite receiving a corrective order under Article 19 (3) of the Act for violating Article 16 (2) 2 of the Act, fails to comply with it without just cause | Article 25 (2) of the Act | 100 / 200 / 300
(c) Where a school meal service provider, despite receiving a corrective order under Article 19 (3) of the Act for violating Article 16 (3) of the Act, fails to comply with it without just cause | Article 25 (2) of the Act | 100 / 200 / 300
